title: Yusuf in one sitting, part one
hook: Surah 12:1–57, from the dream to the treasury
tomorrow: the brothers walk in, hungry, and don't know him. what will he do?

segments.voice: Yesterday, those who reflect: a sky not made in vain, and no worker's work lost. The line: be patient and steadfast. Today a story that needs every ounce of both.
screen: `BE PATIENT AND STEADFAST.` → `A STORY THAT NEEDS BOTH.`

segments.voice: One final down, more to come. Jordan is on Amira's floor eating chips when she sees what Amira's reading for her nightly page: Surah Yusuf. "Yusuf, like your dad?" Then she reads a line and sits up. "Wait. Dreams, jealous brothers, a pit, Egypt? That's Joseph. Joseph with the coat. He's in the Qur'an too?" Jordan grew up with him in Sunday school. Amira grew up with him at Dadi's knee. Same boy, two tellings.
screen: `YUSUF, LIKE YOUR DAD?` → `JOSEPH WITH THE COAT?` → `SAME BOY, TWO TELLINGS.`

segments.voice: Surah Yusuf calls itself, in Pickthall's words, "the best of narratives," and it's told whole, in one surah. Part one runs like this. Yusuf dreams that eleven stars, the sun and the moon bow down to him. His father Ya'qub tells him: don't tell your brothers, or they'll plot against you. They plot anyway. They drop him into a well, and bring home his shirt with false blood on it. Ya'qub answers with words Dadi still says: "comely patience." Yusuf is sold into Egypt, resists the temptation of his master's wife, is proven innocent by a shirt torn from behind, and is jailed anyway. In prison he reads dreams, until the king's dream sets him over the storehouses of the land. Now Jordan's telling, Genesis, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren; and they hated him yet the more." Shared: the dreams, the jealous brothers, the pit, Egypt, the rise. The Torah, the Christian Bible and the Qur'an all carry this boy. And the honest difference: in Genesis, Joseph tells his brothers. In the Qur'an, his father says don't. Genesis gives him a coat of many colors; the Qur'an gives him a shirt that turns up again and again. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. Neither telling needs the other to be wrong.
screen: `THE BEST OF NARRATIVES.` · `DON'T TELL YOUR BROTHERS.` · `THE WELL, THE SHIRT, THE PRISON.` · `HE TOLD IT TO HIS BRETHREN.` · then, large: `THE BEST OF STORIES.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person you've envied lately, even a little. Hold their face for the sit and, instead of measuring yourself against them, quietly wish them one good thing. Jealousy started this whole story; let it stop with you.
screen: `ONE PERSON YOU'VE ENVIED.` · `WISH THEM ONE GOOD THING.`

options: No fight. You're both right: in Genesis he tells them; in the Qur'an, Ya'qub says don't.
She's mixing it up. It's the same story, so the details have to match yours.
